K. M. S. DISSANAYAKE, J.
Instant application has been made to this Court by the Petitioner by
presenting a petition, together with an affidavit and the documents annexed
thereto, marked ‘P1’ to ‘P15’ in support thereof, under and in terms of section
9(1)(c) of the Contempt of a Court, Tribunal or Institution Act No. 08 of 2024
(hereinafter called and referred to as “the Contempt of Court Act”) to be read
with Article 105(3) of the Constitution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of
Sri Lanka (hereinafter called and referred to as “the Constitution”) urging that
Rule be issued against the Respondent to appear before Court and show cause
as to why she should not be punished for the charge of contempt of Court for
knowingly, filing false and misleading affidavits in case No.
CA/WRIT/0565/2021 thereby, misleading this Court and interfering with the
due administration of justice, as morefully, enumerated in his petition. The
learned President’s Counsel for the Petitioner was heard in support of the
instant application and hence, the order today.
In the light of the averments contained in the petition presented to the Court
by the Petitioner, the contemptuous acts alleged to have been committed by
the Respondent which had according to the Petitioner, constituted Contempt
of Court, have arisen out of the evidence adduced by the Respondent on
affirmation in her affidavits dated 16.06.2022 and 10.10.2023 in an action
bearing No. CA/WRIT/0565/2021 brought by the Petitioner before this Court
designating the Respondent hereto, as the 4th Respondent thereto, and the
Petitioner sets out the alleged contemptuous acts in the petition, particularly,
in paragraphs 35 to 53 thereof, and they may be briefly, set out as follows;
Acting on instructions from the Respondent, the Counsel for the
Respondent had made representations before this Court in the said Writ
application specifically asserting that the Respondent never, ever had any
Page 3 of 23
dealings with the Petitioner who being the Notary Public who executed the
Deed of Transfer in question referred to in the petition and denied having
called him at any time whether over the phone or otherwise; and that the
Petitioner verily believes that the Respondent's said denial, made in her
affidavits under oath and through counsel, was a deliberate falsehood, and
intended to mislead this Court, on the presumption that the lapse of nearly a
decade would have precluded the Petitioner from producing any proof or
corroborative material in support of his assertion; and that however, in direct
response to the Respondent's false denial, the Petitioner tendered to this
Court incontrovertible and official call detail records (CDRs) (P3 and P4), duly
certified by the respective telecommunications service providers, Mobitel and
Dialog pertaining to the mobile numbers of both the Petitioner and the
Respondent and they (P3 and P4) conclusively, establish that a telephone call
did in fact originate from the Respondent's number (0718084195) to the
Petitioner's number (0777578359) on the 12th of November 2010, precisely
as pleaded in the Petition; and that the production of those CDRs (P3 and P4)
irrefutably disproves the Respondent's denial and substantiates the
Petitioner's claim that the Respondent had improperly interfered with his
professional duties as a Notary; and that upon being confronted with the
aforesaid incontrovertible documentary evidence, the Respondent, in a
subsequent affidavit filed in the same proceedings, deliberately altered her
position and advanced a new, misleading, and manifestly false version of
events with the intent of deceiving this Court; and that having earlier
unequivocally denied ever placing any call to the Petitioner, she thereafter
averred that she was "unaware whether a third party had used such device to
contact and/or approach the Petitioner," thereby seeking to evade
responsibility for her prior false denial; and that the Respondent failed to
make any contemporaneous complaint from 07.02.2011, being the date on
which the Petitioner duly, informed the Criminal Investigation Department of
the said telephone call requesting that the Deed not be registered, to the
Police, the Bar Association, the Supreme Court, or the Judicial Service
Commission, on the ground that the allegation was false and unfounded; and
that, the Respondent has not stated that she made any inquiry from her
Page 4 of 23
father, her husband, or any other person as to whether they had used her
telephone, nor has any affidavit been filed asserting that any such inquiry
was made; and that telephone records (P3 and P4) further establish that on
the same day and within the same time-frame, calls were made from the
Respondent's telephone to close family members, all routed through the same
cellular tower location which establishes that the Respondent was in
possession and control of the telephone at the material time; and that, the
length, timing, and context of the said conversation are wholly, inconsistent
with the Respondent's subsequent sworn position that she had no
involvement in the transaction, had not contacted the Petitioner, or that some
unidentified third party may have used her telephone; and that, in light of
these events, the Respondent could not reasonably have forgotten either the
telephone call made by her on 12 November 2010 or the prolonged and
confrontational conversation with Muralitharan on 13 November 2010; and
that the Respondent's sworn denial of the telephone call, followed by her
shifting explanation that an unidentified third party may have used her
device, is therefore a deliberate and calculated falsehood advanced to evade
responsibility for her own misconduct; and that, at all material times,
including on 12 November 2010 and at the time of swearing the affidavit
referred to above, the Respondent was a State Counsel attached to the
Attorney General's Department of Sri Lanka and by reason of her office and
legal training, the Respondent was fully aware of: a) her legal obligation to
state the truth on oath; b) the evidentiary nature of affidavits tendered to
court; and c) the serious consequences of making false statements to court;
and that the Respondent knew, or at the very least had reason to believe, that
her statements denying the telephone call and denying knowledge of the
transaction were false; and that the Petitioner respectfully submits that the
aforesaid conduct of the Respondent constitutes a serious affront to the
authority of this Court and amounts to a grave contempt of court, in that she
has wilfully attempted to mislead the Court through inconsistent and false
statements made under oath; and that making a false representations to this
Court knowing them to be false amounts to Contempt of Court as it directly,
interferes with the administration of justice; and that hence, the essential
Page 5 of 23
elements of giving false evidence are present, namely; a) a legal obligation to
state the truth on oath; b) the making of statements which were false in fact;
and c) knowledge of their falsity or belief that they were untrue; and that the
offence of contempt of court is complete once a wilful falsehood with a
tendency to mislead is placed before court, irrespective of whether the attempt
ultimately succeeds; and that, the Respondent's conduct discloses a
calculated attempt to obstruct this Court from arriving at a correct judicial
determination;
It is in this factual context, I would now, propose to examine the law governing
the offence of Contempt of Court in Sri Lanka.
Article 105(3) of the Constitution enacts thus;
“(3) The Supreme Court of the Republic of Sri Lanka and the Court of
Appeal of the Republic of Sri Lanka shall each be a superior court of
record and shall have all the powers of such court including the power
to punish for contempt of itself, whether committed in the court itself
or elsewhere, with imprisonment or fine or both as the court may deem
fit. The power of the Court of Appeal shall include the power to punish
for contempt of any other court, tribunal or institution referred to in
paragraph (1)(c) of this Article, whether committed in the presence of
such court or elsewhere:
Provided that the preceding provisions of this Article shall not prejudice
or affect the rights now or hereafter vested by any law in such other
court, tribunal or institution to punish for contempt of itself.”
As provided for by the proviso to Article 105(3) of the Constitution, Contempt
of Court Act was enacted by the Parliament, conferring upon such other
Court, Tribunal or Institution the power and/or the authority to punish for
contempt of itself.
The preamble to the Contempt of Court Act reads thus;
Page 6 of 23
“An act to provide for the uniform application of the law relating to the
contempt of a court, tribunal or institution; to provide for the procedure
in punishing the contempt of a court, tribunal or institution; and to
provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.”.
Section 2 of the Contempt of Court Act sets out the objects of the Act as
follows;
“The objects of this Act shall be to-
(a) uphold the dignity and authority of a court, tribunal and institution;
(b) protect the due administration of justice;
(c) ensure adherence to judicial directives;
(d) preserve and maintain the effectiveness and impartiality of a court,
tribunal and institution;
(e) strike a balance between the right of expression, fair comment and
compliance with judicial directives;
(f) set out with precision the ambit of contempt of a court, tribunal
and institution; and
(g) ensure the observance of, and respect for, the due process of law.”
[Emphasis is mine]
In terms of section 2(f) of the Contempt of Court Act, one of the key objectives
of the Act is to set out with precision the ambit of contempt of a court,
tribunal and institution; [Emphasis is mine]
As provided for by section 2(f) of the Contempt of Court Act, section 3 thereof,
lays down that, certain acts enumerated therein are deemed to be contempt
of a court, a tribunal or institution and it may be re-produced as follows;
“(1) Save as provided for in any other written law and subject to the
provisions of the Constitution, any person who commits an act or
omission with intent to-
Page 7 of 23
(a) bring the authority of a court, tribunal or institution and
administration of justice into disrespect or disregard; or
(b) interfere with, or cause grave prejudice to the judicial process
in relation to any ongoing litigation,
commits contempt of a court, tribunal or institution, as the case may
be.
(2) Save as provided for in any other written law and subject to the
provisions of the Constitution, any person who does any of the following
acts commits contempt of a court, tribunal or institution, as the case
may be-
(a) wilful disobedience to any judgment, decree, direction, order,
writ or other process of a court, tribunal or institution;
(b) wilful breach of an undertaking given to a court, tribunal or
institution;
(c) expressing, pronouncing or publishing any matter that is false
which, or doing any other act which-
(i) scandalizes or lowers the judicial authority or dignity of
a court, tribunal or institution;
(ii) gravely prejudices, or unlawfully interferes with, the due
course of any judicial proceeding; or
(iii) interferes with, or obstructs the administration of
justice;
(i) use of any electronic device or other instrument for audio
or visual recording or both, in a court, tribunal or
institution, or bringing into a court, tribunal or institution
any such device or instrument for the purpose of audio or
Page 8 of 23
visual recording or both, without the leave of the court,
tribunal or institution already obtained;
(ii) publication or transmission of an audio or a visual
recording or both, of a proceeding or part of a proceeding
of a court, tribunal or institution made by means of any
electronic device or other instrument, or any such
recording derived directly or indirectly from such device or
instrument without the leave of the court, tribunal or
institution already obtained;
(iii) use of any electronic device or other instrument, or
publication or transmission of an audio or a visual
recording or both, of a proceeding of a court, tribunal or
institution, in contravention of any leave granted under
sub-paragraph (i) or sub-paragraph (ii); or
(iv) tampering, altering or falsifying any audio or visual
recording or both, of a proceeding of a court, tribunal or
institution; or
(e) scandalizing a court, tribunal or institution, or a judge or
judicial officer with intent to-
(i) interfere with the due administration of justice;
(ii) excite dissatisfaction in the minds of the public in regard
to a court, tribunal or institution; or
(iii) cast public suspicion on the administration of justice.”
Section 6(1) of the Contempt of Court Act sets out the powers of the Supreme
Court and the Court of Appeal to punish contempt of itself whether committed
in its presence or hearing or elsewhere.
Section 6(1) thereof, enacts that; “The Supreme Court and the Court of Appeal
shall have the power to punish for contempt of itself, whether committed in
its presence or hearing or elsewhere.”.
Page 9 of 23
Section 6(2) thereof, enacts that;
“Where the Supreme Court or the Court of Appeal, as the case may be, in the
exercise of its jurisdiction as referred to in subsection (1), takes cognizance-
(a) of contempt of court committed in its presence or hearing, the
Supreme Court or the Court of Appeal shall hear and determine such
matter in accordance with the procedure set out in section 8; and
(b) of contempt of court committed otherwise than in its presence or
hearing, the Supreme Court or the Court of Appeal shall hear and
determine such matter in accordance with the procedure set out in
section 9.”
Section 9 of the Contempt of Court Act sets out the procedure where Contempt
of Court is not in the presence of the Supreme Court or the Court of Appeal
and it enacts thus;
“9 (1) The Supreme Court or the Court of Appeal, as the case may be,
may take cognizance of contempt of court committed against it, or in
disrespect of its authority, other than contempt of court committed in
its presence or hearing, on-
(a) its own motion;
(b) a motion filed by the Attorney-General, together with any
document or thing in support of the motion; or
(c) a motion filed by any other person, together with an affidavit
and any document or thing in support of the motion.
(2) Every motion or affidavit filed under subsection (1) shall set out the
particulars of the contempt of court alleged to have been committed by
the person alleged to have committed the contempt of court.
(3) The Supreme Court or the Court of Appeal, as the case may be, shall,
after perusing the motion, and the affidavit, document or thing filed
under subsection (1) and satisfying itself that a prima facie case of
Page 10 of 23
contempt of court has been established against the person alleged to
have committed such contempt-
(a) cause a rule to be issued on such person signed by the
Registrar of the Court, giving particulars in writing of the
contempt of court with which he is charged;
(b) direct that such rule, together with a copy of the document
filed under subsection (1), be served personally on such person;
and
(c) fix a date for the hearing of the charge.
(4) On the date fixed for the hearing of the charge, the Attorney-General
may lead the evidence of such witness relevant to the document filed
under subsection (1), if necessary, subject to the right of cross-
examination of the person charged with contempt of court.
(5) On the date fixed for the hearing of the charge, the person charged
with contempt of court shall be afforded an opportunity to make his
defence to the charge and shall be entitled to file an affidavit or to
adduce evidence in his defence.
(6) The Supreme Court or the Court of Appeal, as the case may be, shall
hear and determine the charge after considering the affidavit filed by
the person charged with contempt of court or after hearing the evidence
adduced by such person, as the case may be.
(7) Pending the determination of a charge under this section, the
Supreme Court or the Court of Appeal, as the case may be, may direct
that-
(a) the person charged with contempt of court under this section
be detained in such custody as it may specify; or
(b) such person be released on bail subject to such conditions as
it may deem fit to impose.”
Page 11 of 23
The Petitioner in the averments in the petition, more particularly, in
paragraphs 35 to 53 thereof, alleges that the Respondent has committed the
offence of Contempt of Court as enumerated therein, under and in terms of
the provisions of the Contempt of Court Act.
In light of the matters so averred by the Petitioner in the petition as
enumerated above, the contemptuous acts alleged to have been committed by
the Respondent that would according to the Petitioner, constitute the
contempt of this Court, appear to come within the ambit of section 3(1)(a) and
(b) of the Contempt of Court Act.
Hence, the threshold issue that would now, arise for our determination at this
juncture, is whether this Court can satisfy itself upon a careful perusal of the
application together with the affidavit and the documents annexed thereto,
made to this Court by the Petitioner under section 9(1)(c) of the Contempt of
Court Act that a prima facie case of Contempt of Court as enumerated by
section 3(1) (a) or (b) of the Contempt of Court Act, has been established by
the Petitioner in his petition against the Respondent alleged to have
committed such contempt as required under section 9(3) of the Contempt of
Court Act.
If this threshold issue can be answered in the affirmative only, this Court will
cause a rule to be issued on the Respondent singed by the Registrar of this
Court giving particulars in writing of the contempt of court, tribunal or
institution with which he or she is charged as the case may be, as required
by section 9(3)(a) of the Contempt of Court Act. [Emphasis is mine]
It is in this context, let me re-produce section 3(1) (a) or (b) of the Contempt
of Court Act which reads thus;
“(1) Save as provided for in any other written law and subject to the
provisions of the Constitution, any person who commits an act or
omission with intent to-
(a) bring the authority of a court, tribunal or institution and
administration of justice into disrespect or disregard; or
Page 12 of 23
(b) interfere with, or cause grave prejudice to the judicial process
in relation to any ongoing litigation,
commits contempt of a court, tribunal or institution, as the case may
be.”
The contemptuous acts constituting contempt of court as alleged by the
Petitioner in his petition and as enumerated above, may be summarized as
follows;
The Respondent has wilfully attempted to mislead the Court through
inconsistent and false statements made under oath as enumerated above; and
that making such false representations to this Court knowing them to be false
amounts to Contempt of Court as it directly, interferes with the
administration of justice, and hence, the Respondent's conduct discloses a
calculated attempt to obstruct this Court from arriving at a correct judicial
determination.
Under section 3(1) of the Contempt of Court Act, a court, tribunal or
institution should satisfy itself that, alleged act or omission has been
committed by a person “with intent to” bring the authority of a court,
tribunal or institution and administration of justice into disrespect or
disregard; or interfere with, or cause grave prejudice to the judicial process in
relation to any ongoing litigation. [Emphasis is mine]
Hence, it becomes manifest that, for the proper constitution of an offence of
contempt of court under section 3(1) of the Contempt of Court Act, court,
tribunal or institution must satisfy itself not only of the falsity of the statement
made by the person alleged under oath or affirmation but also, must satisfy
itself that, the false statement had been made by that person “with intent
to” bring the authority of a court, tribunal or institution and administration
of justice into disrespect or disregard; or interfere with, or cause grave
prejudice to the judicial process in relation to any ongoing litigation.
[Emphasis is mine]
Page 13 of 23
Let me next, deal with the binding judicial precedents relevant and pertinent
to the matter at hand.
In Asnar vs. Andrew 15 NLR 406, the appellant was, at the conclusion of
the case, charged by the commissioner for giving false evidence by stating on
oath or affirmation that the defendant signed the plaintiff’s book when the
account was looked into. The appellant admitted that his statement was
untrue but stated, to quote his own words, “I admit that I lied but it happened
a long time ago.” On that, the learned Commissioner convicted him under
section 800 of the Civil Procedure Code and sentenced him to two months
rigorous imprisonment. It was held by the Supreme Court in appeal as
follows;
“Now it has been held several times in this Court that a mere false
statement on oath does not amount to a contempt of court punishable under
section 800 of the Civil Procedure Code. A false statement may in ‘some cases’,
be so transparently, false as to be disrespectful to the Court and so amount
to a contempt. But a false statement unaccompanied by any special
circumstances of this nature does not amount to a contempt of court within
the meaning of part LX of the Civil Procedure Code.”
In Wickramasekera vs. Dingiri Banda 16 NLR 458, the appellant, who was
a witness, appealed from an order of the District Judge convicting him of
contempt of Court and imposing on him a fine of Rs. 100. The alleged
contempt, according to the District Judge, consists in prevarication. He
records that the appellant is charged with "contempt of Court by trying to
mislead it by prevarication," and the prevarication referred to here is thus set
forth by the District Judge:." That he, on the 16th instant, denied that the
Tambligahawatta, which had been transferred to him by a notarial deed, had
been so transferred by the first defendant, and stated that she had no
connection whatever with that transaction. It was held by the Supreme Court
in appeal that,
“Now, deliberate prevarication no doubt, constitutes contempt of Court;
but what is prevarication, and was the appellant guilty of prevarication, or
Page 14 of 23
merely of making a false statement when giving evidence on oath? To
prevaricate literally means to shift or turn from one side to the other. As
commonly used, it means to evade telling the truth, to shuffle, to quibble.
The underlying idea is an artful mode of escaping the scrutiny of an
inquirer by the use generally of loose and indefinite expressions. This
being so, it is. quite clear that the appellant was not guilty of
prevarication. He was asked a certain question, and he gave a clear and
definite though false answer. That was not prevarication, and it follows that
the conviction on the ground of prevarication cannot stand. Can it be said
that the appellant is guilty of contempt in giving false evidence? A Judge
cannot be too careful and cautious in proceeding as for contempt against
a witness who generally gives false evidence. If this course is freely
pursued, some one witness or another may have to be punished for
contempt of Court in almost every case. Ordinarily, a witness who gives
false evidence in a Court of justice intends no contempt. Intention may,
however, be presumed, and the witness may be guilty of contempt if the
evidence is so transparently false as to give rise to a reasonable suspicion
of an attempt on the part of the witness to trifle with the Court. The
position is clearly laid down by the Chief Justice in the case of Asanar v.
Andrew. I cannot say that the answer given by the witness in the present case
was evidence of the description mentioned above. I say nothing of the possible
ways in which the witness might have been dealt with. I set aside the order
appealed from. [Emphasis is mine]
The Petitioner states that the Respondent should be charged with contempt
of Court by trying to mislead this Court by prevarication, and the
prevarication referred to by the Petitioner in the instant application is thus,
set forth by him in his petition, more particularly, in paragraphs 35 to 53
thereof as morefully, enumerated above, in that it was alleged that, the
Respondent has wilfully attempted to mislead the Court through inconsistent
and false statements made under oath as enumerated above; and that making
such false representations to this Court knowing them to be false amounts to
Contempt of Court as it directly, interferes with the administration of justice,
Page 15 of 23
and hence, the Respondent's conduct discloses a calculated attempt to
obstruct this Court from arriving at a correct judicial determination.
Hence, in the instant application too, the alleged contempt, according to the
Petitioner, consists in prevarication.
It is my view that, the prevarication is implicit in section 3(1) of the Contempt
of Court Act too, inasmuch as the legislature deliberately, uses therein, the
phrase “with intent to” as being direct and essential corollary for the
constitution of a charge of contempt of court thereunder, for; as a general rule
a mere utterance of a false statement under oath or affirmation alone, would
not amount to contempt of court under section 3(1) of the Contempt of Court
Act, unless, it is accompanied by a clear intention to bring the authority of a
court, tribunal or institution and administration of justice into disrespect or
disregard; or interfere with, or cause grave prejudice to the judicial process in
relation to any ongoing litigation for; the Legislature in incorporating the
phrase “with intent to” into the section 3(1) of the Contempt of Court Act
clearly, intended that it was so as being direct and essential corollary for the
constitution of a charge of contempt of court thereunder. [Emphasis is mine]
Hence, it becomes manifest upon a careful scrutiny of section 3(1) of the
Contempt of Court Act and the binding judicial precedents of the Supreme
Court as cited above, that, two essential ingredients must be present at the
same time for the constitution of an offence of a contempt of court under
section 3(1) of the Contempt of Court Act, namely;
a) Commission of an act or omission;
b) Commission of an act or omission as such must be in such a
nature that the person alleged to have committed the offence of a
contempt of a court, tribunal or institution, had by the
commission of the alleged act or omission, clearly, and
unequivocally, intended to bring the authority of a court, tribunal
or institution and administration of justice into disrespect or
disregard; or interfere with, or cause grave prejudice to the
judicial process in relation to any ongoing litigation.
Page 16 of 23
Now, the pertinent question is whether this Court has satisfied itself after a
careful perusal of the petition, verifying affidavit and the documents annexed
thereto, that a prima facie case of contempt of court has been established by
the Petitioner against the Respondent alleged to have committed such
contempt.
The Petitioner describes in his petition “the act or omission” alleged to have
been committed by the Respondent, to be the Respondent’s wilful attempt to
mislead this Court through inconsistent and false statements made by her
under oath as morefully, enumerated in his petition by the Petitioner as being
the first direct and essential corollary for the constitution of a charge of
contempt of court under section 3(1) of the Contempt of Court Act specified
under limb a) above.
And, the making of such false statements by the Respondent to this Court in
the said action knowing them to be false thereby, directly, interfering with the
administration of justice, thus, obstructing this Court from arriving at a
correct judicial determination in the said case, has been described by the
Petitioner therein, as being the second direct and essential corollary for the
constitution of a charge of contempt of court under section 3(1) of the
Contempt of Court Act as specified under limb b) above.
Now, the pertinent question would be; Is the Respondent guilty of
prevarication by making those two statements on oath?.[Emphasis is
mine]
It may now, be examined.
The Petitioner had in paragraph 29 of the petition dated 06.11.2021 (P13)
presented by him to the Court of Appeal in instituting the said case bearing
No. CA/WRIT/565/2021, stated as follows;
“The Petitioner states that on or around 12.11.2010, the Petitioner
received a telephone call from the 4th Respondent, the daughter of the
3rd Respondent requested him not to tender the Deed of Transfer
bearing no. 320 for registration stating that the Vendor has not been
Page 17 of 23
paid the full consideration. The Petitioner explained to her that he could
not consider his request as he had act in the best interest of his client
and safeguard his right to priority by registration.”.
Apparently, in response to the averments so contained in paragraph 29 of the
petition dated 06.11.2021 (P13) the Respondent had in paragraph 5(c) of her
affidavit dated 10.06.2022, that had been furnished to the Court of Appeal in
the said case, stated as follows;
“I have never ever called the petitioner nor met him in his capacity
as a notary public”.
In response to averments in paragraph 5(c) of the affidavit of the Respondent,
the Petitioner had in paragraph 41 of the counter-affidavit dated 21.01.2023
(P13) presented by him to the Court of Appeal in the said case bearing No.
CA/WRIT/565/2021, stated as follows;
“Answering paragraph 5 of the said Statement of Objections of the 4th
Respondent, I reiterate paragraph 29 and 30 of the Petition and state
that the 4th Respondent called me on the 12th of November 2020 and
requested me not to tender the said deed of transfer for registration for
the reason that the vendor has not paid the full consideration. I
informed her that I cannot accede to her request as I have to act in the
best interest of my client. I specifically deny the averments contained in
paragraph 5 (d) and I state that to the best of my knowledge and belief
that the 4th Respondent's mobile number is 0718084195. This is
evidenced by the telephone directory issued by the Attorney General's
Department in the year 2015. A true copy of the relevant telephone
directory containing the 4th Respondent's name and mobile number is
annexed hereto marked 'X1'. My mobile number is 0777578359. This
is evidenced by a mobile bill issued in my name marked as 'X2'. A copy
of a mobile payment receipt relating to the mobile no. 0718084195
which is registered under the name of the 4th Respondent is marked as
X3. I state that the 4th Respondent called me from her mobile no.
0718084195 to my mobile no. 0777578359 on the 12th of November
Page 18 of 23
2010. The call lasted for two minutes and twenty-four seconds. By way
further answer, I state that the 5th Respondent had made a complaint
to the Periyaneelavani Police Station on 26th November 2022 alleging
that an undue influence had been exerted on the Notary relating to the
said land transactions. Consequent to the said complaint, the Police
had filed a B report No. B/940/22 in the Magistrate's Court of
Kalumanait with a view to carry out an investigation under the
supervision of the Learned Magistrate of Kalmunai. Thereupon, the
police requested the said Learned Magistrate to issue an order directing
for a detailed report pertaining to the mobile number 0718084195
relating to the month of November 2010. Consequent to the said order,
SLT Mobitel (formerly Sri Lanka Telecom) has filed a report setting out
in detail of telephone calls of the outgoing and incoming calls relating
to the said mobile number namely 0718084195 with regard to the
month of November 2010. I annex hereto a certify copy of the case
record in case no. B/940/22 containing the incoming and outgoing
calls in with regard to mobile number 0718084195 which is registered

Hence, the Respondent in her further affidavit dated 10.10.2023, had while

However, a careful perusal of the position so adverted to by the Respondent

Furthermore, she had therein, adverted to a position that she was unaware

marked as P3 and P4 which were heavily relied on by the Petitioner in support
of the assertion so made by him as enumerated above.
With regard to the position so adverted to by the Respondent in her further

itemized telephone call records marked as P3 and P4 which were heavily

In view of the foregoing, it clearly, appears that the Petitioner has not
furnished material to this Court in proof of his assertion as enumerated
above, which are necessary for this Court to satisfy itself that, a prima facie
case of contempt of Court has been established against the Respondent

thereunder, in determining as to whether rule should be issued or not under
section 9(3)(a) thereof.

In the circumstances, it clearly, appears that, the Petitioner has not
established that the sworn statement made by the Respondent in her further
affidavit furnished to Court in the said case, namely; she had never ever called
the Petitioner on the day in question, was a false statement made on
affirmation and therefore, the Respondent's sworn denial of the telephone call,
followed by her shifting explanation that an unidentified third party may have
used her device, was a deliberate and calculated falsehood advanced to evade
responsibility for her own misconduct which constitutes a serious affront to
the authority of this Court and amounts to a grave contempt of court, in that
she had wilfully attempted to mislead the Court through inconsistent and
false statements made under oath; and that making a false representations
to this Court knowing them to be false amounts to Contempt of Court as it
directly, interferes with the administration of justice.
There remains a further point for our consideration and it may now, be
examined.
It was the position of the Petitioner that the Respondent's sworn denial of the
telephone call, followed by her shifting explanation that an unidentified third
party may have used her device, was a deliberate and calculated falsehood
advanced to evade responsibility for her own misconduct which constitutes a
serious affront to the authority of this Court and amounts to a grave contempt
of court, in that she had wilfully attempted to mislead the Court through
inconsistent and false statements made under oath; and that making a false
representations to this Court knowing them to be false amounts to Contempt
of Court as it directly, interferes with the administration of justice.
Upon a careful perusal of the petition filed by the Petitioner in the said case
P13, it clearly, appears that even though the Respondent hereto, had been
made 4th Respondent thereto, no relief whatsoever, had been sought from her
by the Petitioner in prayer thereto, hence, it clearly, appears that, the
Respondent was neither a necessary party nor a proper party to the said writ
application in terms of the law.
Page 22 of 23
In the circumstances, it clearly, appears that no case had been made out by
the Petitioner against the Respondent in the said case for her to meet or to
defend even though she had been made a mere party thereto, by the
Petitioner. Hence, it clearly, appears that the Respondent had been a mere
spectator in the said case.
In these state of facts and circumstances, can it be said that, the Respondent
had any reason to make a deliberate falsehood on affirmation in her further
affidavit furnished to the said case with the intent to mislead the Court
through alleged inconsistent and false statements made under oath thus,
directly, interfering with the administration of justice? I think not in view of
the reasons stated above.
It cannot thus, be said that, the Respondent is guilty of prevarication by
making those two statements on oath.
In view of the foregoing, I would hold that the Petitioner had totally, failed to
establish the two ingredients a) and b) as enumerated above-the direct and
essential corollary for the constitution of a charge of contempt of court
namely; a) Commission of an act or omission; b) Commission of an act or
omission as such must be in such a nature that the person alleged to have
committed the offence of a contempt of a court, tribunal or institution, had by
the commission of the alleged act or omission, clearly, and unequivocally,
intended to bring the authority of a court, tribunal or institution and
administration of justice into disrespect or disregard; or interfere with, or
cause grave prejudice to the judicial process in relation to any ongoing
litigation.
In the circumstances, I would hold that this Court has not satisfied on the
material furnished to it by the Petitioner that, a prima facie case of contempt
of Court has been established against the Respondent alleged to have
committed such contempt as required by section 9(3) of the Contempt of Court
Act-the threshold issue to be satisfied by this Court thereunder, in
determining as to whether rule should be issued or not under section 9(3)(a)
thereof.
